the phonological store has a capacity of around 1.5-2.0 seconds for the storage of phonological forms, and that the rehearsal process is effective in extending the retention of phonological information beyond this limit.

the phonological similarity effect is a robust phenomenon in the recall of both words and pictures, that it is unaffected by the type of material presented for rehearsal, that it is not a function of the type of response used to measure recall, and that it is present in both adults and children, in both normal and neuropsychological populations.

the phonological similarity and phonological loop effects are both present when words are learned in isolation, but the similarity effect is absent and the loop effect reduced when words are learned within a context.
